reachable: Yes, at the scored read position, and I verified it by execution rather than reading. (1) Group membership is exactly as claimed: the router group is precisely {ref_q (128,768), ref_k (128,768), ref_p (64,768), ref_keybias (1,768), ref_null (1,768)} and nothing else — cmd_proj/obs_proj/read_to_h are (176,768) and excluded by 176>128, ref_own is (1,944), ref_diff (1,64), ref_gate (1,179), tr_read/ref_read (768,768), all verified against the built net. (2) These parameters feed ref_contrib, which is added to pred_cmd at EVERY command position including the final lone read command; the reference closure at position i reads only registers j<i, so it is NOT gated on the read step having an observation — the failure mode that was fatal earlier in this search does not apply here. (3) Gradient: at init the router group receives EXACTLY zero gradient (measured grad_absmax = 0.0 for ref_q/ref_k/ref_p/ref_keybias/ref_null/ref_own/ref_gate/ref_recency, backward taken from the last command position only), because ref_read is zero in both weight and bias and g_ref multiplies that zero — the author's central premise is correct, and stronger than stated (ref_gate is starved too). Only ref_read.weight/bias get gradient at init (2.1e-3 / 2.5e-3), so the ramp-in story is real. After perturbing ref_read.weight off zero, the router group does receive gradient from the scored read position alone (ref_q 3.5e-4, ref_k 3.7e-4, ref_p 6.5e-4, ref_keybias 3.9e-3, ref_null 1.6e-3), so the group is not permanently dead. (4) The two mechanisms are exactly as described and exactly aligned: with steps=4000, warm=160 (4%), decay_start=1360 (34%), window=1000, decay_end=3000 (75%); the router group sits at a constant 2x base (1e-3) with weight_decay 0.0 after warmup for the whole run; the trunk and Muon groups are flat at the floor over precisely the same last 1000 optimizer steps that the Polyak window averages. The averaged copy fires: harness _train calls opt.step() exactly `steps` times, and I verified numerically that after the final step the live parameters equal the true uniform mean of the last `window` post-update iterates to float precision (max abs difference 3.6e-7), that the mean is genuinely different from the last iterate (ref_q max abs 1.6e-4), and that the spectral cap is re-applied to the two (768,768) readouts afterwards.
solves_outside_model: No. The optim impl reads nothing but parameter tensor shapes (ndim, shape[0], shape[1]) — no data, no command strings, no labels, no filesystem state. It cannot route information about the move chain anywhere. The genome does import the partner's stream r3_srcdst_hashslot_coding, which does parse command strings, but it is a legitimate re-encoding: _compact(cmd) is a pure function of ONE command string, hashing that command's own source path, destination path, verb and seven form flags into fixed disjoint coordinate blocks (SRC [0,352), DST [352,704), VERB [704,752), flags 752..758 — all verified in source, exactly as the hypothesis states). It never sees another step, an observation, or filesystem state, so it hands the model the operands and never the resolution; composing source-of-i against destination-of-j across steps remains the model's job. The read command's token is a function of the read path alone, identical under the native and role-swapped chains. This is the legitimate side of the line, not the retracted shape.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says, and the parts an inventor without torch could most easily have gotten wrong are right. Verified by execution: the router group is exactly the five reference-closure scorer tensors and nothing else; it runs at a constant 2x base lr with weight_decay 0 for the entire run after warmup; the trunk and Muon groups cosine-decay to a floor at 75% of the budget and sit flat over precisely the window the Polyak average covers; the uniform iterate mean is accumulated post-update and post-spectral-projection and IS copied into the live parameters on the final optimizer step (matching a hand-computed mean to 3.6e-7), with the cap re-applied. The central premise — that the reference scorer gets literally zero gradient at initialization because ref_read is zero-initialized — is exactly true when measured (all router grads 0.0 at init; only ref_read gets signal), and the group becomes reachable from the scored read position once ref_read moves off zero. The mechanism is not observation-gated at the read. Every incidental shape claim checks out (cmd_proj/obs_proj/read_to_h (176,768); ref_own (1,944); ref_diff (1,64); ref_gate (1,179)), as does the data claim: in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl sequence 0, step 14 cats /tmp/w/cups/g53/f149.tmp, step 19 mv's it to magic.txt.1 with empty output, step 22 cats magic.txt.1 and gets the step-14 content back — literally the case described. Three divergences, all minor: the Muon group is six tensors not five (sys_val.weight rides along; identical to the parent, so no behavior change); floor_ratio is silently raised from the parents' effective 0.05 to 0.10, an unstated third change to the schedule the prose blames, which confounds the head-to-head against the parent; and the "exactly the own=1 special case" equivalence used to justify dropping r22 is approximate, not exact. What I could NOT check: anything about whether this moves comp_ca. I did not run the real eval, the probe, or the GPU lane. The Polyak-Ruppert variance argument is imported from constant-step SGD theory and is untested here for AdamW + Muon + a post-step spectral projection, whose iterates are not the trajectory that theorem is about; whether the hot router converges into one basin over the tail, and whether the averaged point beats the last iterate, are open. The author flags all of these as unmeasured. Note for interpretation, not a defect in the code: the parent scored -0.0037 against a measured noise floor of 0.0227, so a single run cannot separate these mechanisms from noise, and the added stream (r3) makes explicit source/destination structure available, which is also what a move-order-position predictor would key on — read the result against the reported analytic band.

divergences.claim: "The parent's Muon selector is untouched and still picks the five bias-free (64,176) addressing extractors (file_read, file_write, path_read, path_write, tr_path) via the same sibling rule."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The selector (identical to the parent's, so behavior is unchanged) picks SIX tensors, not five: file_read.weight, file_write.weight, path_read.weight, path_write.weight, tr_path.weight AND sys_val.weight, all (64,176). sys_val is nn.Linear(d=176, sys_d=64) — it is not an addressing extractor and it is not bias-free (only its .weight is routed). The author's enumeration of the Muon group is wrong; the selector itself is as described.
divergences.evidence: Built the genome's net and reproduced the selector: MUON keys (6): file_read.weight, file_write.weight, path_read.weight, path_write.weight, sys_val.weight, tr_path.weight — all (64,176). r24 line 105: self.sys_val = nn.Linear(self.d, self.sys_d) with sys_d=64, d=176. No behavioral divergence from the parent (r18's selector picks the same six).

divergences.claim: The prose frames the parent's trunk schedule as the problem — "warmup ends at 4%, the hold ends at 34%, and from there the learning rate falls to 5% of base" — and describes the change as (a) a hot constant-lr router group and (b) a Polyak-averaged constant-step tail.
divergences.what_the_code_does: It also doubles the trunk floor. r18 (both parents, no optim params in either genome) defaults floor_ratio=0.05; this impl defaults 0.10 and genome.json pins 0.10. Every non-router parameter therefore trains the whole post-cosine tail at 2x the parent's floor lr. That is a third, unstated change bundled into the paired comparison against the parent, and it is exactly the knob the prose singles out as the parent's defect.
divergences.evidence: r18_spectral_capped_transition_readout.make(... floor_ratio=0.05 ...) vs candidate make(... floor_ratio=0.10 ...); genome.json optim params floor_ratio 0.10. Measured trunk lr with steps=200: 5.000e-04 base -> 5.000e-05 flat tail (= 0.10x). Discoverable in genome.json, never stated in hypothesis.txt.

divergences.claim: "r22's prefix-content cross-attention ... is exactly the own=1 special case of r24's closure (registers = own*OBS, pulled = A OBS, injected through the zero-init ref_read behind sigmoid(ref_gate))." Used to justify dropping r22 from the crossover.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The zero-init (D,D) readout behind a sigmoid gate matches, but the scoring input does not: r22 scores its attention from the d=176 post-transformer hidden (self.xq/self.xk = nn.Linear(self.d, xattn_dim)), while r24 scores from ref_ln(cmd_raw) at full D=768 width; r22 also injects after the sysfilm styling, r24 before it. "Exactly" overstates a near-equivalence. This concerns a mechanism the crossover discards, not the submitted code.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/arch/r22_prefix_content_xattention.py lines 29-34 (xq/xk over self.d, x_out zero-init (D,D)) and its DESCRIPTION "AFTER the sysfilm styling"; vs r24 lines 135-137 and 475-495 (ref_q/ref_k over ref_ln(cmd_raw) at D, ref_contrib added to pred_cmd before the g_sys/b_sys styling).
